newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen flat or slightly down.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen flat or slightly down.

text.p: Polish shares fell after Monday's slight gain and analysts said the market would likely maintain its slight downtrend this week during the public offering of the copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA.

They said a good sign was the prime minister's Tuesday statement that 1998 GDP could rise five to six percent versus the government's previous forecast of 5-5.5 percent, but heavy buying should not ensue before September's parliamentary poll.
"There are lots of macroeconomic signals that could have a positive influence but it seems the elections ballast restricts bourse investment," said Mateusz Andrzejewski of Pekao house.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.5 percent to 15,087.9 points and turnover rose 33 percent to 211.8 million zlotys on both markets.

Analysts also said there still remained some negative economic signals, including a central banker's statement last week that Poland faced a Czech-style financial crisis in 1998 if it failed to balance next year's budget.
They said the summer season was also likely to dampen buying but that the market could rise toward 15,500 points this month after the KGHM offering.
Bank Handlowy rose 1.6 percent to 38.5 zlotys in heavy trade and could continue rising gradually toward 40 zlotys before profit-taking falls begin, analysts said.
They said the bank's 105.9-million-zloty turnover on Tuesday, nearly half the session's main market trade, reflected larger investors taking up shares sold by smaller.
Handlowy, one of Poland's largest firms, started trade on Monday 8.3 percent above issue at 37.9 zlotys.
Other large-cap banks were mixed on Tuesday with Gdanski and Slaski the top gainers but BRE down 3.6 percent.
